close_reason: No-op resolution: defense of the existing parse_request contract — the function operates on pre-parsed serde_json::Value so it physically cannot enforce byte-size caps. The transport-less posture is intentional and consistent with workspace PLAN.md. The new doc block on parse_request already enumerates the three caps the HTTP integration MUST apply. Closing as a no-op; the defended shape stays.
description:
Why this choice is correct: parse_request operates on a pre-parsed serde_json::Value, so it cannot enforce byte-size or JSON-nesting-depth caps. Rather than silently inheriting unbounded input, the new doc block (parse.rs:28-55 from commit 3aad685) explicitly enumerates the three caps the HTTP integration MUST apply: body size, JSON nesting depth, and per-pointer recursion (which IS enforced internally, lines 197-208).

What a future contributor might incorrectly suggest changing: 1) Add a byte-size cap parameter to parse_request — but the function takes Value, not bytes, so it physically cannot enforce byte size after the JSON parse has already allocated. The right place is the HTTP layer (axum / hyper / warp), and the doc names each idiomatic mechanism for the three popular options. 2) Refactor parse_request to take raw bytes and own the JSON parse — but that couples the JMAP-protocol layer to serde_json::from_slice, defeats users who want to feed pre-parsed Values (e.g. WebSocket frame consumers), and duplicates the body-size enforcement that the HTTP framework already has.

The contract-as-doc shape is the right kit-vs-product line. The kit defines the JMAP protocol surface; the product (kith, stoa, jmap-testjig, or third-party consumer) brings the HTTP framework and the body-size config. The PLAN.md and workspace AGENTS.md repeatedly state this transport-less posture. parse_request explicitly defending the line with three named limits is defensive engineering, not laziness.
title: parse_request DoS-limit contract documented as caller-responsibility rather than enforced
